pageCache.text:
Headteachers Welcome
Welcome to Oaklands Primary Academy
Every pupil matters, every moment counts
I am the proud Head of School at Oaklands Academy Biggin hill. The staff here at Oaklands are truly amazing, their passion for learning and their drive to always ensure the children achieve their best is inspirational. Oaklands Academy is proud to be part of Chancery Education Trust. This is a multi academy, educational Trust with high aspirations and a collaborative approach to ensuring all children receive the best possible education.
One of the core principles guiding my leadership is the belief that every child deserves to feel welcomed and supported at school. My goal is for every student at Oaklands Primary School to leave Year 6 feeling like they have reached their full potential. This involves not only academic excellence, but also developing critical life skills, creativity and sparking a lifelong love of learning.
Our five core values at Oaklands Academy are: Respect, Resilience, Responsibility, Resourcefulness and Risk Taking. There is a feeling of these values in all that we do and we celebrate children who show them in all aspects of their lives, inside and outside of the school gates. We have an expectation that all children are polite and courteous and that they embody these values in all that they do.
Community engagement and open communication are central to my approach. I am committed to playing a major part in our local community and ensuring that Oaklands Academy remains a place where all students feel valued, encouraged and motivated to achieve their best. I believe that a strong partnership between the school and parents is crucial for student success. I maintain transparent and regular communication with all parents and encourage their involvement in school activities. Their insights and feedback are invaluable as we strive to create the best possible educational experience for all our students.
Every day is a new day at Oaklands and I am personally excited to walk through the door every morning to see the plethora of activities that are going on around the school and the vibrant curriculum that is being taught.
I look forward to welcoming you all in person to Oaklands, but in the meantime, please look around our website and social media and if you would like a tour please contact the school office and we will be happy to accommodate.

Ethos, Visions & Values
Ethos, Visions & Values
Through our strong family ethos, the Trust, staff, parents, governors and friends of Oaklands Primary Academy are committed to working together to provide the highest quality of education that will meet the needs of every child and enable them to achieve their personal best.
Our Ethos
Oaklands Primary Academy enables everyone to be proud of their achievements by:
Encouraging everyone to do their very best
Our Vision
At Oaklands Primary Academy children strive to achieve their best in a secure and stimulating environment. We provide a happy, healthy community where everyone can develop confidence, respect for others and a love of learning. At the heart of everything we do are the ‘five Rs’:
Resilience
Respect
Resourcefulness
Responsibility
Risk-taking.
Our Aims
Our teaching, organisation and entire environment are based upon agreed aims and values which underpin the work of the Academy. These aims are:
To deliver a curriculum which ensures children acquire and develop:
To develop and maintain a climate of:
Through working together within the Academy community, we encourage children to develop positive moral values and qualities and become progressively more aware of themselves as responsible members of the Academy community. We ensure that the academy environment is one within which the children feel valued as individuals, have confidence in their own capabilities and are encouraged to develop their own talents and interests as much as possible. In this way, each child is personally enriched and able to contribute to a changing and developing society. Every child is given equal opportunity to benefit from a broad and balanced curriculum, which actively involves children in their learning and promotes the highest possible standards of academic achievement. We encourage children to respect others and promote high standards of behaviour and courtesy towards their peers and adults. This includes respect for everyone’s race, religion and culture, gender and physical ability.

pageCache.pageTitle: SMSC and British Values - Oaklands Primary
pageCache.text:
SMSC & British Values
At Oaklands Primary Academy we uphold and teach pupils about SMSC & British Values which are defined as:
• democracy • rule of law • individual liberty • mutual respect • tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs
These values are taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health and Emotional (PSHE), Religious Education (RE), Philosophy for Children and Citizenship. We also teach SMSC & British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum.
The academy takes opportunities to actively promote SMSC & British Values through assemblies and whole school systems and structures such as electing and running a successful Pupil Parliament and School Council. We ensure that our curriculum planning and delivery includes real opportunities for exploring these values. Actively promoting SMSC & British Values also means challenging pupils, staff or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values, including ‘extremist’ views.
Democracy is an important value at our academy. Pupils have the opportunity to have their voices heard through our School Council. The elections of members of the School Council and of Year 6 House Captains are based on pupil votes.
Children recommend each other for the half termly “Values Awards” which are awarded to individual children (or classes) who show they are modelling co-operation, respect, morality, empathy, adaptability, trust, communication and resilience.
The children have worked together to form and understand the 3Cs, co-operation, common sense and courtesy, the children work and live by the 3Cs and they are displayed around the school alongside the Golden Rules.
The importance of laws and rules, whether they are those that govern the class, the academy or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days. Our ‘Golden Rules” for behaviour are aligned to an agreed set of codes and if children are given verbal warnings this is always set against the agreed school behaviour policy. Children are asked to identify which Golden Rule they have broken to ensure that this connection is made and understood. Gold stars have been introduced to reward children for living their life by the chosen set of rules. Their names are entered into the Golden Book and they are given a Golden star during celebration assembly. Children are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the police, fire service, lifeguards etc. are regular parts of our calendar and help reinforce this message.
Tolerance of Those of Different Faiths and Beliefs:
This is achieved through enhancing pupils’ understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity in our local community which is by large white British. Assemblies and discussions involving prejudices and prejudice-based bullying have been followed and supported by learning in RE, PSHE and the International Primary Curriculum where explicit International Learning Goals are taught through themed topics. Different cultures, values and beliefs are celebrated and discussed throughout the topics.

Music Knowledge Organisers
Music Curriculum
Intent
Our Music curriculum aims to help every child feel musical and develop a lifelong love of music. We want pupils to become confident performers, composers, and listeners, while learning to appreciate music from different cultures, traditions, and times. Through music, children also develop important transferable skills such as teamwork, creativity, and confidence, which support learning across the curriculum and beyond school life.
Implementation
Music is taught through the Kapow scheme, which provides a clear progression of skills across the school. Lessons include singing, listening, playing instruments, improvising, composing, and learning musical notation. Children have access to a wide range of instruments, including class sets of glockenspiels and recorders, so they can experience practical music-making.
Music is embedded in school life through weekly singing assemblies, performances, and enrichment opportunities. We also have two school choirs, giving pupils the chance to perform and develop their vocal skills further. Lessons are planned to be inclusive and engaging, with activities that allow all children to succeed while providing challenge for those ready to go further.
Impact
By the time children leave Oaklands, they will be confident performers, composers, and listeners who can express themselves musically. They will understand key musical concepts such as pitch, tempo, dynamics, and structure, and be able to use musical vocabulary accurately. Pupils will appreciate a wide range of musical styles and understand how music reflects cultural and historical contexts. Our approach ensures children develop creativity, confidence, and a love of music that will stay with them throughout their lives.
